utterances.text: Tab 143. In these instructions, in point 3, does it say during the activity exclusively target -- targets outside settled areas or where you know for sure where there are no civilians, no civilian population, where it is established with certainty that there is no civilian population.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says in point 3 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in point 1 it says activity against terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So if in point 1 it says that targeted should be terrorist forces exclusively and in point 3 that they underline that targets should be in areas where there is -- are no civilians, what can we draw -- what conclusions can we draw from that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we can clearly deduce from that that this dispatch relates to preparing all the elements necessary for acting against terrorist groups exclusively outside inhabited settled areas and exclusively where there could be no consequences on the civilian population, so once the conditions are ripe. And as we can see in continuation, the positions are clearly defined and determined, positions at which such targets exist, and those positions have been established on the basis of intelligence data or information supplied by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. Thank you. You already pointed out in your answer to a question that was put to you by Mr. Robinson or by Mr. Bonomy, I cannot say exactly now, that in principle the police were never the first to open fire.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, since we've gone through these questions related to the use of force, after everything that is -- that you said, can it be stated that the MUP forces resorted to disproportionate use of force? I bear in mind the principle of proportionality that you quoted as one of the principles involved in the use of force.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already given that in my answer related to Mr. Ashdown's transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, can we go back to paragraph 3, just the instruction that fire must be directed solely at targets outside populated areas or where it is reliably known that there is no civilian population. What would happen if KLA personnel were intermingled with civilian population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have given a partial answer to that question already. The police always refrained from taking any kind of active measures against groups that might have included civilians, even if there were -- was any shade of doubt. Such action could be taken only if it can unequivocally be proved that a group includes terrorists only. I can say with reliability that this order was never carried through because it was impossible to determine ever that a group included terrorists only. This was used during planned terrorist actions when the target could clearly be discerned, that is to say that it could be established there were no civilians there, of course honouring the principle I've already explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, just a few questions that have to do with legality in the work of the police. Since you were there yourself, you saw for yourself how the police operated. You were at the MUP staff several times, at meetings as instructed by your minister, as you already mentioned. Tell us, during 1998 and 1999, did the police and army act lawfully or not?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During 1998 and 1999, the police in general acted lawfully. When I say "in general," I'm saying that there are exceptions, isolated individual cases when certain individual policemen did not abide by regulations. That is why I'm saying "in general."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I allow the witness to answer that question because it arguably relates to fact issues as well, but ordinarily it will be a legal question on which he is not competent to comment. We have to stop at 1.43. There is another case here. So the last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of a case, any case, of an unlawful order or carrying out an unlawful order or any other kind of unlawful action that was not punished, or, rather, of any unlawful action with regard to which criminal proceedings were not instituted?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to give a very precise answer: I'm not aware of a single case of anyone issuing an unlawful order or that anyone carried out that kind of order. I am also not aware that anyone planned or instigated or tolerated anyone's behaviour in terms of unlawful conduct. Also, I'm not aware of a single case of anyone having carried out an unlawful deed without having measures taken against him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are going to stop here, but I must say that in assessing the weight to be attached to that question, we will take account of the fact that no evidence has been given to show that this witness has any competence to comment on the lawfulness of an order. We are adjourned until tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, as a high official of the police who was authorised and who is one of the authorised officials in terms of implementing the law, he has to know exactly what is lawful and what is not lawful. Otherwise, he could not carry out his official duty. His official duty was to implement the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No evidence has been given to support that. We are adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
